editorial:
If you grew up watching Jackie Chan movies, this one feels like a warm hug with a few hard punches. Ride On follows a washed-up stuntman who has spent his whole life doing dangerous work for little pay, and his loyal stunt horse who has been right there beside him through it all. When debt collectors show up and the two fight them off in a wild, clumsy brawl, the whole thing goes viral online. Suddenly this forgotten stuntman is famous again, but the attention also brings old problems back into his life. The movie mixes laughs, heart, and real stunt work in a way that feels old-school and fresh at the same time.

The action scenes are the real highlight, with Jackie Chan still doing impressive physical comedy and stunts. The horse is surprisingly charming and gets some of the best moments. The story can feel a little scattered at times, and some jokes land better than others, but the emotional core keeps you invested. If you love classic Jackie Chan energy, this is a fun watch.
endingExplained: In the final act, the stuntman faces a big public stunt show where everything could go wrong. His daughter finally understands how much he sacrificed for his craft and shows up to support him. The twist is that the viral fame was never the real goal; it was just a way to reconnect with his family. The horse gets a happy ending too, staying with him. The movie closes on a warm, emotional note about loyalty and second chances.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Jackie Chan action and heartwarming family stories.
